refuters.argument:
After a clause-by-clause search I could not find a polygon on which the printed def:regular and the Lean CV.Regular / CV.principalTurn (as pinned by CV.RegularData) disagree, nor a printed clause without a field, nor a field that adds or narrows content on the printed domain. Verdict: faithful.

Clause (A), spec of τ_i (source lines 4-7 of the excerpt): CV.PrincipalTurnSpec L i τ (statement file 167-171) is literally (−π<τ ∧ τ<π) ∧ cos τ = planeDot(edge L (i−1), edge L i)/(euclideanLength·euclideanLength) ∧ SignType.sign τ = SignType.sign(det …). Primitives checked: edge P i = P(i+1) − P i (SM/Polygon.lean:49) = δ_i with the incoming/outgoing pair δ_{i−1}, δ_i at corner q_i; planeDot = u1v1+u2v2 (EuclideanPlane.lean:27); euclideanLength u = sqrt(u1²+u2²) (EuclideanPlane.lean:29,31-34, the Euclidean |·|, not the product norm); det = u1v2 − u2v1 (Polygon.lean:16); SignType.sign is Mathlib's ordinary sgn (if 0<a then 1 else if a<0 then −1 else 0; Mathlib/Data/Sign/Defs.lean:266). Field principal_turn_spec (266-271) pins exactly this. principalTurnSpec_iff is Iff.rfl against SM.PrincipalAngleSpec (PrincipalAngles.lean:9-12), which is the same formula.

"the unique τ_i": field principal_turn_unique (273-274). "principal turn" as an object: CV.principalTurn L i := principalAngle(edge L (i−1))(edge L i) = arg(conj(δ_{i−1})·δ_i) (RegularPairs.lean:54); field principal_turn_value (276-279) asserts it satisfies the spec and is the unique solution under RegularPair, i.e. exactly when the printed turn exists.

"It exists precisely when δ_i is not a negative multiple of δ_{i−1}" (8-9): field exists_iff (281-282): (∃! τ, spec) ↔ edge(i−1)≠0 ∧ edge i≠0 ∧ ¬Kink. The two nonzero-edge conjuncts are the standing polygon hypothesis of (A) ("Let L be a closed polygon", with d_i ≠ 0 by def:polygon) made explicit because the Lean fields are stated on every LabelledTuple c; restricted to polygons the field reads (∃! τ) ↔ ¬Kink, exactly the printed sentence. This is a conservative widening (stronger), not a narrowing.

"if det ≠ 0 it is nonzero" (9): field nonzero_of_det (284-286). The extra RegularPair hypothesis is implied by det ≠ 0 (det ≠ 0 forces both vectors nonzero and non-collinear), so nothing is lost. "if δ_i is a positive multiple of δ_{i−1} it is 0" (9-10): field zero_of_positive_multiple (288-290) with hypothesis edge(i−1) ≠ 0 (polygon context). Kernel-checked probe_zero_turn: for u ≠ 0, RegularPair u (2•u) ∧ principalAngle u (2•u) = 0 — so a flat (zero-turn) corner is regular with turn 0 in both readings. CV printed says only "if" (SM says "exactly when"); Lean gives only "if", matching CV.

Kink (10-12): CV.Kink L i := ∃ r<0, edge L i = r • edge L (i−1) (178-179) is literally δ_i ∈ ℝ_{<0}δ_{i−1}; field kink (293-295) records the definition and that no τ satisfies the spec at a kink. The printed gloss "the two candidate values ±π are both excluded from the open interval" is the reason no τ exists (cos τ = −1 forces τ = ±π, outside (−π,π)); the Lean records its definitional consequence rather than the reason. I judge this explanatory, not a lost clause.

Clause (B) (13-17): CV.Regular P := (∀ i, edge P i ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ i (l:ℝ), 0<l → edge P (i+1) ≠ (−l) • edge P i (184-185) is word-for-word "d_i ≠ 0 for all i and d_{i+1} ≠ −λ d_i for all i and all λ>0"; regularLocus n = {P | Regular P} ⊆ LabelledTuple n = ZMod n → ℝ² = (ℝ²)^n for n ≥ 3 (188); field regular_locus (298-300). "Equivalently, every principal turn of clause (A) exists": field regular_iff_turns_exist (302-303), Regular P ↔ ∀ i, ∃! τ, spec. The `3 ≤ n` hypotheses on these two fields are CV's own standing assumption (def:polygon "Let n ≥ 3"), not an SM narrowing; the definitions themselves are unrestricted and the general theorems (258-260) hold for all n.

Relation to SM (fields regular_iff_sm 305, principal_turn_eq_sm 307-308): SM.Regular P := ∀ i, RegularPair(edge P (i−1))(edge P i) (RegularLocus.lean:12-13), RegularPair u v := u≠0 ∧ v≠0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, v = r•u (RegularPairs.lean:8-9); re-indexing i ↦ i+1 and l = −r gives CV.Regular ↔ SM.Regular — the two printed loci are the same set. SM.principalTurn (RegularLocus.lean:15-16) is definitionally CV.principalTurn. Name resolution inside namespace CV with `open SM` picks CV.Regular / CV.principalTurn first (resolveUsingNamespace precedes open decls), so `Regular P ↔ SM.Regular P` relates the two intended objects.

The specific disagreement cases I hunted for: (1) antiparallel consecutive edges (kink): printed — no turn, P ∉ 𝓡_n; Lean — Kink holds, exists_iff/kink give no τ, Regular fails (edge(i) = r•edge(i−1), r<0 violates the second conjunct with l = −r). Agreement. (2) zero turn (positive multiple): both allow it in the locus with turn 0. Agreement. (3) zero edge: both exclude from 𝓡_n; Lean additionally records no turn exists (outside the printed domain, harmless). The only thing a reader should know is that CV.principalTurn is a total function with junk values off the printed domain — kernel-checked probe_kink_junk: principalAngle u (−u) = π for every u ≠ 0 (and arg 0 = 0 at a zero edge) — whereas the printed turn is undefined there. No bundle field asserts anything about principalTurn at a kink (principal_turn_value is guarded by RegularPair, and kink asserts non-existence of a spec value), so this is the standard Lean total-function convention, not a discrepancy in what is claimed. No field is weaker than, or adds content to, the printed definition on its domain.
